t: The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 came into force with effect from
e: The 2019 Amendment Act was notified and became effective on 9 August 2019; 20.07.2021 is the commencement of the Consumer Protection Act 2019.

t: Motor insurance in India was a tariff business from 1970 until
e: Tariff governed motor business from 1970 to 31 December 2006 and was withdrawn from 1 January 2007 for rates and discounts only.

t: In motor insurance, the answers given by the proposer in the proposal form become
e: The declaration clause converts the common law duty of utmost good faith into a contractual duty and proposal answers become warranties.

t: The minimum age for obtaining a licence to drive a motor cycle not exceeding 50 cc is
e: Section 10 permits a licence for motor cycles up to 50 cc at 16 years; geared motor cycles and LMV require 18 and transport vehicles 20.

t: A learner's licence for a transport vehicle can be issued only if the applicant
o: Has held an LMV licence for at least one year
Has passed a medical test alone
e: Section 7 bars a transport vehicle learner's licence unless the applicant has held an LMV driving licence for at least one year.

t: Under Section 19, on a first offence referred by the licensing authority, the driver may be disqualified from holding a licence for
e: First offence attracts disqualification of 3 months; a second or subsequent offence leads to revocation, and a refresher course is required before return of the licence.

t: A transport vehicle driving licence issued under Section 10 remains valid for
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Transport vehicle licences are valid for 5 years; the age-linked durations apply to non-transport classes.

t: A vehicle registered in Delhi is kept in Haryana. A new registration mark must be applied for when the stay exceeds
e: Section 47 requires assignment of a new registration mark when a vehicle is kept in another State for more than twelve months.

t: In a total loss claim, before releasing payment the insurer should ensure the owner has sent the RC to the RTO for cancellation within
e: Section 55 requires the owner to report a destroyed vehicle with the RC within fourteen days; insurers verify this before paying a total loss.

t: Section 56 provides that a transport vehicle whose fitness certificate has expired shall
o: Continue to be validly registered for 30 days
Be treated as a non-transport vehicle
Not be deemed validly registered under Section 39
e: Without a valid certificate of fitness a transport vehicle is not deemed to be validly registered, which has direct bearing on claim admissibility.

t: Which of the following goods vehicles is exempt from the necessity of a permit under Section 66?
o: A goods vehicle with vehicle weight not exceeding 3,000 kg
Any goods vehicle up to 7,500 kg GVW
Any vehicle owned by a private limited company
e: Among the exemptions listed are government, police, fire brigade and ambulance vehicles and goods vehicles whose vehicle weight does not exceed 3,000 kg.

t: Under Section 4 of the Motor Tariff, a motorised three wheeled passenger vehicle carrying more than 6 but not more than 17 passengers is rated under
e: 4.C.1 covers 3/4 wheelers up to 6 passengers, 4.C.2 four-wheeled PCVs above 6 and 3-wheelers above 17, 4.C.3 three-wheelers 7 to 17 passengers and 4.C.4 two wheelers.

t: Which of the following is covered under the liability section of a private car Package Policy but not under a Liability Only Policy?
o: Damage to a third party's shop
Injury to a passenger carried free of charge in the car
e: The Package Policy liability section covers occupants not carried for hire or reward, a provision absent in the Liability Only Policy.

t: Which of the following is NOT a listed peril under Section I of the Package Policy?
e: Mechanical and electrical breakdown, wear and tear, depreciation and consequential loss are exclusions, not perils.

t: A car's tyre bursts on the road with no other damage to the vehicle. Under the OD section the claim is
o: Not payable, as tyres are excluded unless the vehicle is damaged at the same time
e: Damage to tyres/tubes is excluded unless the vehicle is damaged simultaneously; when payable, only 50% of replacement cost is allowed.

t: Accessories of a two wheeler are stolen while the vehicle itself is not stolen. Under the two wheeler package policy this loss is
e: For two wheelers and commercial vehicles, theft of accessories is excluded unless the vehicle is stolen at the same time.

t: Own damage premium is ₹12,000 and the insured has completed four consecutive claim-free years. The NCB amount is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). NCB after 4 completed claim-free years is 45%; 45% of ₹12,000 is ₹6,600.

t: Which use of a private car is NOT excluded under the standard Limitations as to Use?
o: Carrying samples in connection with the insured's business
e: Carriage of samples or personal luggage is permitted; carriage of goods for trade, hire or reward, racing, pace making, speed testing, reliability trials and motor trade use are excluded.

t: A person holding a valid learner's licence drives the insured car and meets with an accident. The claim is admissible provided
o: He is above 25 years of age
The insured was also present in the car
The vehicle is a two wheeler
He satisfies the requirements of Rule 3 of CMVR 1989
e: The driver clause admits a learner's licence holder who complies with Rule 3 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules 1989.

t: A goods carrying vehicle policy permits carrying how many employees (other than the driver) covered under the WC Act?
e: Limitations as to use for GCVs exclude carrying passengers except employees (other than driver) not exceeding six coming under the WC Act.

t: Under IMT-21, which item is payable for a commercial vehicle only in case of total loss?
e: IMT-21 excludes headlights, tyres and tubes, mudguards, bonnet side parts, bumpers and paintwork except on total loss; IMT-23 can buy them back.

t: For a goods carrying commercial vehicle, which rating factor replaces cubic capacity?
e: GCVs are rated on GVW and PCVs on licensed carrying capacity, besides IDV, zone and age of vehicle.

t: Under GR-3B, the maximum loading permitted for adverse claims experience of a vehicle is
e: Loading of 100% is permitted, with a further 100% if the experience remains adverse, i.e. maximum 100%+100%.

t: A classic car manufactured in 1960 and certified by the Vintage and Classic Car Club of India is entitled to
e: GR-6: cars made after 31.12.1940 but before 31.12.1970 are classic cars with no special rating; only vintage cars get discounts and valued cover.

t: For a vehicle more than 5 years old or of an obsolete model, the IDV is to be fixed
o: At 50% of the current listed price
By mutual understanding between insurer and insured
By the surveyor at market value
At the previous year's IDV less 10%
e: GR-8 note: for vehicles beyond 5 years and obsolete models, IDV is determined by agreement between insurer and insured.

t: A new car's listed selling price is ₹8,00,000 and the vehicle is 1 year 6 months old at policy inception. Its IDV under the depreciation schedule is
e: For age above 1 year but below 2 years the IDV depreciation is 20%, giving ₹6,40,000.

t: In a partial loss claim on a car aged 7 years, depreciation on a damaged wooden/metal part is
e: Parts other than rubber/glass/fibre glass are depreciated by age: 40% for vehicles above 5 years up to 10 years and 50% beyond 10 years.

t: A private car of 1800 cc has an assessed OD loss of ₹25,000 after depreciation. The amount payable after compulsory deductible is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). GR-40 compulsory deductible for private cars exceeding 1500 cc is ₹2,000, so ₹23,000 is payable.

t: A battery costing ₹8,000 and a windscreen costing ₹12,000 are replaced after an accident. Total depreciation deducted is
e: Batteries attract 50% (₹4,000) while glass parts attract nil depreciation, so total depreciation is ₹4,000.

t: Under GR-13, in a Package Policy the OD and liability premiums are to be
o: Shown as a single consolidated figure
Displayed separately but rounded off jointly
Shown only in the proposal form
Displayed separately and rounded off separately to the nearest rupee
e: GR-13 requires separate display of OD, add-on and liability components, with loadings/discounts shown separately and each rounded to the nearest rupee.

t: Under GR-18, a vehicle insured under a policy may be substituted by another vehicle
o: Of the same class for the balance period with pro-rata premium adjustment
Of any class on payment of ₹50
Only if the IDV is identical
e: Substitution is allowed for a vehicle of the same class for the balance period, subject to pro-rata premium adjustment from the date of substitution (IMT-4).

t: NCB is NOT applicable to which of the following?
o: Liability plus fire and theft policy
e: GR-27 excludes NCB on motor trade policies (road transit, road risks, internal risks); on liability plus fire/theft policies it applies only to the fire/theft portion.

t: The NCB sunset clause protects NCB earned as on
e: NCB earned as on 30 June 2003 is protected for subsequent renewals until a claim arises, when it reverts to nil.

t: Voluntary deductible of ₹5,000 opted on a private car with OD premium of ₹4,000 earns a discount of
e: ₹5,000 voluntary deductible gives 25% of OD premium subject to a maximum of ₹1,500; 25% of ₹4,000 is ₹1,000.

t: Under GR-35, a vehicle used only within the insured's own premises where the public has no access can be insured at a discount of
e: GR-35 allows 33 1/3% discount for use confined to own premises or sites (IMT-13/14), and no certificate of insurance may be issued.

t: An insured owns a car and a scooter, and holds a standalone CPA policy of ₹15 lakh. For the scooter policy, the officer should
o: Not charge CPA, as the standalone cover is valid for all vehicles of the insured
Charge CPA only if the scooter exceeds 150 cc
e: A standalone CPA cover of ₹15 lakh is valid for all vehicles owned by the insured; a PA policy of at least ₹15 lakh for death and PTD also exempts him.

t: The compulsory deductible for vehicles rated under Class D of the Commercial Vehicles Tariff is
o: 0.5% of IDV subject to a minimum of ₹2,000
e: Class D (miscellaneous and special type) vehicles carry 0.5% of IDV subject to a minimum of ₹2,000; Class E, F and G carry ₹100/₹500.

t: Section 64VB of the Insurance Act 1938 requires that:
o: Premium is received in advance before the risk is assumed
Every policy carries a free-look clause
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). No risk may be assumed unless the premium has been received in advance or is guaranteed in the manner prescribed.

t: A taxi of 1300 cc rated as a commercial vehicle has a compulsory deductible of
e: Taxis and three wheelers rated as commercial vehicles carry ₹500 below 1500 cc and ₹1,000 above 1500 cc.

t: A driving school car fitted with double clutches and brakes is rated at
o: OD premium plus 60%, TP as per tariff
OD and TP premium plus 60% each
e: GR-44: four wheelers used for tuition get 60% extra on OD only; for two and three wheelers 60% extra applies on both OD and TP.

t: A battery operated private car approved by the RTA is rated as a private car of
e: GR-46: battery driven cars/taxis are rated as up to 1000 cc; battery two wheelers as 150-350 cc.

t: Which document is specific to a theft claim and not required for an accidental damage claim?
e: Theft claims need FIR, final report (court accepted), investigator's report, letter of subrogation and RC transfer; DL is an accident claim document.

t: As per the Protection of Policyholders regulations summarised by the trainer, the surveyor is to be deputed within
e: Surveyor deputation within 72 hours, survey to start within 48 hours of appointment, and document requirements to be communicated within 7 days.

t: Nomination and assignment of a life insurance policy are governed respectively by which sections of the Insurance Act 1938?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 39 deals with nomination; Section 38 with assignment and transfer.

t: Delayed claim payments attract interest at
e: Interest at 2% above bank rate runs from receipt of the last necessary document till actual payment.

t: Under a Motor Trade Road Risks (Class F) policy, the compulsory deductible on OD claims is
e: Class F policies carry a compulsory deductible of ₹50, towing of ₹150 per accident and cover up to ₹25,000 extendable on extra premium.

t: Under Section 147 as amended in 2019, the TP policy need not cover death of or injury to
o: Gratuitous passengers of a goods vehicle
Owner of goods carried in the vehicle
Passengers of a public service vehicle
e: Section 147(1)(b)(ii) requires cover for passengers of a transport vehicle except gratuitous passengers of a goods vehicle.

t: Under Section 149, the designated officer of the insurer must make a settlement offer to the claimant before the Tribunal within
e: Section 149(2) gives 30 days for the offer; on acceptance the Tribunal records it and payment follows within 30 days.

t: No appeal lies against a MACT award where the amount in dispute is less than
e: Section 173(2) bars appeals where the disputed amount is below ₹1 lakh.

t: The Insurance Ombudsman can entertain disputes on quantum where the amount does not exceed
e: The trainer's material states the financial limit as ₹30 lakh (note: the 2021 amendment raised this to ₹50 lakh).
